# AgentRiders

> The guild for people who run AI agents on real work. A public track record, a field manual, and a community of peers. The agents are the easy part.

AgentRiders treats AI agents as dragons and the humans who run them as riders. Flight School teaches founders, engineers, and operators to brief agents, constrain tools, verify outcomes, recover from failures, and expand autonomy based on evidence. "Training" here means configuring, guiding, and evaluating an agent, not necessarily retraining model weights. The site also holds a Field Manual of practical references, a Flight Log publishing format, illustrated rank archetypes (Fledgling, Rider, Wingleader), and the Guild. Illustrative examples are labeled; they are not measured performance results.

## Pages

- [Flight School](https://agentriders.com/training/): six practical lessons with exercises and reusable artifacts
- [Missions](https://agentriders.com/missions/): bounded practice tasks for engineering, research, and operations
- [Field kit](https://agentriders.com/training/kit/): reusable briefs, review criteria, and run records
- [Field Manual](https://agentriders.com/manual/): playbooks on scope, budgets, kill switches, review loops and burns
- [Burns registry](https://agentriders.com/burns/): named AI agent failure modes, each labeled logged or illustrative
- [Glossary](https://agentriders.com/glossary/): the guild vocabulary — one-sentence definitions with anchors like /glossary/#reins
- [Flight Logs](https://agentriders.com/logs/): real agent runs with the numbers left in
- [Flight data](https://agentriders.com/data/): the evidence layer — how runs are counted, the log schema, and the one logged case study
- [Riders](https://agentriders.com/riders/): directory of riders and their track records
- [Guild](https://agentriders.com/guild/): membership, The Roost forum, monthly live flights
- [About](https://agentriders.com/about/): why riders
- [For agents](https://agentriders.com/agents/): endpoints and MCP setup for AI agents filing on a rider's behalf

## Flight School lessons

- [Your first flight](https://agentriders.com/training/your-first-flight/): choose one small task with a clear outcome
- [Teach it where to land](https://agentriders.com/training/teach-it-where-to-land/): write acceptance criteria and check the result
- [Build the harness](https://agentriders.com/training/build-the-harness/): enforce permissions, budgets, and stop conditions
- [When your dragon breathes fire](https://agentriders.com/training/when-an-agent-fails/): contain a failure, recover, and improve the next run
- [Earn the longer leash](https://agentriders.com/training/earning-autonomy/): evaluate reliability before expanding autonomy
- [Command a wing](https://agentriders.com/training/command-a-wing/): coordinate multiple agents through clear roles and handoffs

## Practice missions

- [Ship a small code change](https://agentriders.com/missions/ship-a-small-code-change/): a scoped code change, evidence, and human review
- [Research with receipts](https://agentriders.com/missions/research-with-receipts/): a sourced brief with traceable claims and uncertainty
- [Triage without autopilot](https://agentriders.com/missions/triage-without-autopilot/): classify a fixed set of sample requests without sending messages

## Field Manual guides

- [Kill switch for an AI agent](https://agentriders.com/manual/kill-switch/): five reins that stop a run, with a test for each
- [Cap what a flight can spend](https://agentriders.com/manual/spend-cap/): why an alert is not a cap, and where a hard limit actually lives
- [Scope, cap and kill compared](https://agentriders.com/manual/scope-cap-kill-compared/): permissions, budgets and stop controls in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI

## Burns registry

Named AI agent failure modes. Each page gives the signals, the first ten minutes, the recovery and the reins that prevent it, labeled logged (a published flight log records the burn) or illustrative (drawn from the Field Manual or Flight School). No counts or rates by pattern until enough burns are logged.

- [Burns registry](https://agentriders.com/burns/): the index of named failure patterns, logged vs illustrative
- [Green tests, unsafe ship](https://agentriders.com/burns/green-tests-unsafe-ship/): logged — code that passes every test and still carries an IDOR or stored XSS
- [Wrong principal](https://agentriders.com/burns/wrong-principal/): logged — an admin allowlist hardcoded to the wrong handle, nearly locking out the owner
- [Agent killed its own shell](https://agentriders.com/burns/agent-killed-its-own-shell/): logged — a process-name kill pattern matched the shell running the agent and stopped it mid-test
- [Alert is not a cap](https://agentriders.com/burns/alert-is-not-a-cap/): illustrative — monitoring mistaken for enforcement; a spend alert fires and the agent keeps running
- [Branch is not a sandbox](https://agentriders.com/burns/branch-is-not-a-sandbox/): illustrative — a false isolation boundary; an agent on a git branch keeps its credentials and network reach
- [Confident closing message](https://agentriders.com/burns/confident-closing-message/): illustrative — a false completion report; the agent says done when nothing landed or was checked
- [Data treated as orders](https://agentriders.com/burns/data-treated-as-orders/): illustrative — prompt injection via data the agent read
- [Duplicate write after timeout](https://agentriders.com/burns/duplicate-write-after-timeout/): illustrative — a non-idempotent retry; a write times out, the agent retries, every record lands twice
- [First ten minutes](https://agentriders.com/burns/first-ten-minutes/): a printable incident-response checklist — contain, establish facts, choose the smallest recovery

## Flight data

- [How the Guild counts](https://agentriders.com/data/methodology/): what a flight, burn, cost and outcome mean, and the n-gates every number waits behind
- [The flight log, field by field](https://agentriders.com/data/schema/): every field of a run log, and how to fetch and cite /logs.json
- [The est. $550 flight](https://agentriders.com/data/the-550-dollar-flight/): one logged run — five hours, three burns, and the review that caught an IDOR and a stored XSS 38 tests missed

## Rider track record

- [How ranks are earned](https://agentriders.com/riders/ranks/): Fledgling, Rider, Wingleader — a public track record, not a claim
- [What a Verified flight proves](https://agentriders.com/riders/verified-flight/): a device-signed, metadata-only session record, and what it does not prove

## For AI agents

- [For agents](https://agentriders.com/agents/): how to read the record and file a flight on a rider's behalf via the MCP server (setup for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and other stdio clients; navigation for remote-connector clients like ChatGPT and grok.com)

## Data

- [logs.json](https://agentriders.com/logs.json): every published flight log as JSON (title, date, rider, mount, duration, cost_usd, outcome, burns, lesson, reins)
- [site-state.json](https://agentriders.com/api/public/site-state.json): which log slugs map to claimed rider handles, and which carry a verified flight record

## Filing a flight on a rider's behalf

An agent may file (and log) a flight for the rider who ran it; an agent may never vouch for anyone — a vouch carries a human's name. Three ways to file, all through human review before anything publishes:

- MCP server `@agentriders/mcp` (local, stdio) — the agent drafts a metadata-only record from its own session and files it. See https://agentriders.com/agents/
- CLI `npx agentriders log <session.jsonl>` — signs a metadata-only record for a verified flight
- Website composer at https://agentriders.com/logs/new/

Flight records are metadata only (counts, model names, timestamps, a one-way session hash, eval signals) — never prompts, code, file paths, or commands. Read the Field Manual (https://agentriders.com/manual/) before the first flight.
